name: Retinol sandwiching

card.summary: A skincare routine that layers retinol between two coats of moisturiser to reduce dryness and irritation so smoother, clearer-looking skin can be pursued with fewer breaks.
card.aka: Retinol sandwich method, retinoid sandwiching, skincare sandwiching
card.note: A 2025 ex vivo study found the full three-layer sandwich reduced retinoid bioactivity about three-fold; moisturiser on only one side did not.

quick.overview:
Retinol sandwiching means applying a layer of moisturiser, then retinol, then another layer of moisturiser. The idea is to buffer the retinol so it sits less harshly on bare skin, which can make it easier to tolerate. For appearance, the payoff is staying consistent with a retinoid, which is used to improve the look of fine lines, roughness and uneven skin texture.

The technique spread on social media, including TikTok. Dermatologists quoted in the press describe it as a way to help patients tolerate a drying ingredient. A 2025 ex vivo study found that the full sandwich reduced retinoid activity about three-fold, while applying moisturiser either just before or just after did not.
quick.how: People apply a light moisturiser to clean skin, then the retinol product, then a second layer of moisturiser, typically in the evening. Some mix the retinol into a heavier moisturiser instead. Dermatologists quoted in coverage describe it as suiting beginners or people with sensitive skin, and some describe a gradual shift to applying the retinoid directly as skin adapts.
quick.risks: The routine itself adds no new ingredients, but retinol can cause redness, scaling, dryness and itching (sometimes called retinoid dermatitis). The buffering layers may reduce how much retinoid reaches the skin. Retinoids are generally not advised in pregnancy, and sun protection is part of standard guidance. Regulatory limits on retinol in cosmetics apply in the EU and UK.

lead: Retinol sandwiching is a skincare method in which a moisturiser is applied, followed by retinol, followed by a second layer of moisturiser, so that the retinol is enclosed between two layers. Some people instead blend retinol into a heavier moisturiser and apply it all at once [1].

People use it to improve the look of skin with a retinoid, which is cosmetically used to reduce the visible effects of skin ageing such as fine wrinkles and roughness [2]. The sandwich is meant to cut the dryness and irritation that can interrupt use, helping someone keep applying retinol long enough to see changes.

The method became popular on TikTok, where related videos have tens of millions of views [1]. Dermatologists quoted in press coverage describe it as a tolerance aid, and a 2025 conference poster examined its effect on retinoid activity [1][3].

chain: Smoother, more even-looking skin over time
angle.text: The sandwich does not itself improve skin; it is a way of making retinol use more comfortable. People use it so they can stay on a retinoid routine that is applied for fine lines, texture and tone.

paras: In the full sandwich, a moisturiser goes on first, retinol second and more moisturiser last. A dermatologist quoted by NBC News said it can help patients tolerate retinol, which can be drying; another described it as creating a sustained-release barrier that slows absorption and reduces irritation [1].

The same coverage quoted dermatologists saying anyone with sensitive skin can try it, that it may help people who want to use stronger retinoids, and that people with darker skin tones may be more sensitive to retinol and could benefit from it [1].

A poster at the 2025 American Academy of Dermatology annual meeting, by Parsa, Li, Patel and colleagues, used human skin explants from a single donor treated for 48 hours with retinol 0.1% or tretinoin 0.025%, alone or with a lightweight moisturiser. Gene-expression markers of retinoid activity (HBEGF, HAS3) were measured by qPCR. A two-step open sandwich, with moisturiser before or after, matched the retinoid alone; the three-step full sandwich reduced activity roughly three-fold. The authors attributed this to dilution and penetration effects. The study was ex vivo, used one donor and was sponsored by Kenvue Brands [3].
No clinical trial in people has compared sandwiching with other routines for visible outcomes or irritation.

Topical retinoids commonly cause redness, scaling, dryness and itching, a pattern described as retinoid dermatitis [2]. Retinol degrades with light, oxygen and heat [2]. Since November 2025 the EU and UK cap retinol in cosmetics at 0.05% retinol equivalent in body lotions and 0.3% in other products, with mandatory labelling [2].

The method is part of wider skincare discussion about retinoid introduction. Participants describe layering moisturiser to reduce flaking and dryness while building tolerance, and some move to an open sandwich or direct application over time.

timeline.event: Poster presented at the AAD annual meeting comparing open and full sandwiches ex vivo; coverage published March 2025 [3].

lore.intro: Retinol sandwiching spread through TikTok and skincare communities as a way to introduce retinoids more gently [1].

claims.claim: Sandwiching retinol lets you tolerate it with less irritation
claims.believers: Proponents and some dermatologists say the moisturiser layers slow absorption and reduce dryness and irritation, especially for sensitive skin [1].
claims.experts: Dermatologists quoted in press coverage support it as a tolerance aid [1], while a 2025 ex vivo study found the full sandwich reduced retinoid activity about three-fold [3].

claims.claim: Moisturiser before or after the retinol (open sandwich) keeps full effect
claims.believers: Users describe applying moisturiser on only one side as a compromise.
claims.experts: In the ex vivo study, open sandwich bioactivity was comparable to the retinoid alone [3].
